## New strongest local execution statement

SourcePruningEnumerationSharedRecursive.finite_complete discharges
ResumeComplete by induction on the actual finite recursive depth.
run_finite_complete_resources exposes the result from current inputs.
The public result has NO smaller-depth execution supplier, future
Context supplier, completed trace or future cache-bound hypothesis.

For any chosen finite recursive depth, a CURRENT Packet, Fits/carrier,
actual edge-selection membership/length rules, current suspended-mass
ceiling and original SharedRecursiveReservation.Reserved produce a
sufficient work bound and ONE actual outcome. Every larger work bound
returns that same outcome through the literal SharedRecursive.run.
The resource result uses the finite forecast computed from that same
original seed, depth and mass ceiling.

The outcome retains its actual caller/query and a coupled full memo/Post
witness. Every emitted output retains its OWN cache, caller, query,
metadata Packet and bounds. A stopped outcome retains its actual reason,
already emitted outputs and optional endpoint. No endpoint is invented
for None. Each full memo witness belongs to the SAME endpoint/Post/query.
The theorem does not equate full memo witnesses across different outputs
or forecasts. It does not prove a whole-driver ordered memo trace.

This is an eventual-stability and resource/Post theorem for the CURRENT
shared recursive model. The model currently selects ordinary Entry
continuations. Unsupported, terminal, Mu/union and exhausted observations
remain real stops where that worker does not support them. This theorem
does not establish complete source normalization, source coverage,
accepted-output meaning, source order or adequate recursive depth.
It does not derive one original-source total-work bound, computed worker
fuel adequacy or capacity at a fixed host width such as 64 bits.

### Actual callback, head and sibling composition

SharedCallbackResources.callback_complete_resources derives the actual
Left recordTypes result from the current Packet and allocated fragment.
It retains one stable raw singleton, updated metadata, framed cache,
RenderStable, Frame, typing/open-hole/type facts and SAME seed resources.
The callback itself does not change the native caller or query memos.

SharedHookInduction defines the legitimate smaller-depth ResumeComplete
hypothesis on CURRENT inputs. callback_induction_complete_resources
invokes it only after the actual callback has returned its updated
metadata and framed cache. Frame.values derives that cache's mass bound.
receipt_induction_complete_resources first derives this CURRENT Packet
from the actual new shared receipt. Callback rejection emits no output.
The arbitrary raw-failure law retains its exact observation and endpoint.

SharedFiniteHeadResources derives the literal captured-edge receipt,
stable head bound, full same-return Post/memos, actual cache bounds and
callback resources from CURRENT decoded target facts and reservation.
It derives selected parent availability/closedness from current realized
data. It does not use an independently supplied prepared parent.

SharedFiniteSiblingResources executes the actual recursive hook BEFORE
the next alternative. Each alternative restores the ORIGINAL captured
enumeration cache and metadata, but receives the actual caller/query and
full memo witness returned by the preceding recursive hook. It retains
per-receipt head bounds, per-output callback-stage bounds and the first
actual stop. A callback stop retains its own outputs and nested reason.
An unsupported head stops at the literal ENTRY caller/query using
Post.refl; the proof does not use the generic head packet's unrelated
existential endpoint to justify that stop.

SharedOutcomeResources derives the original captured-cache Packet from
that actual native Post. finish_resources_general retains arbitrary
stopped outputs and the actual optional endpoint on the NEW shared type.

### Actual prefix and complete depth induction

SharedPrefixResources projects only the actual current prefix facts,
Post, full memo/query witness, cache Packet, headProfile and carrier.
No old finish or old continuation execution is in its public predicate.
The actual Right callback is pure (false, original metadata), so the
returned metadata Packet is the current original metadata Packet.

The complete raw PrefixResult need not be equal at different work fuel:
its prepared action can capture the fuel. checkpoint_resources fixes
the actual branch endpoints and permits an action witness at each bound.
Do not replace this with false equality of the complete prefix value.

SharedFiniteExpansionResources consumes that current checkpoint and
the actual shared sibling scan. Old prefix laws are reused PRIVATELY

SAME unchanged runPrefix. Subsequent caller/cache/final memo/Packet
facts come from ONE new-prefix right_packet bundle. Parked recursion
uses the legitimate smaller-depth hypothesis. Empty retains its reached
endpoint. Nonordinary/terminal entry retains its literal unsupported stop.

SharedZeroOutcomeResources proves every actual zero-depth decision,
including the exhausted expansion receipt. SharedFiniteResources then

nonexpand decisions. Its induction removes the recursive supplier.

### Same original mixed reservation

SharedRecursiveReservation.narrowSeed pays only headProfile for the
actual heap-only prefix. afterHead uses the NEW shared incoming advance,
with original child/guard cost ceilings. step pays that head followed by
its smaller-depth callback. stage iterates this pair in sibling order.
The positive final forecast includes one extra row for parked recursion.
Reserved and the final-Room laws cover every nested scheduled query.

SharedRecursiveReservationBounds proves the actual NEW edge cost fits

it reuses no old executed backend. Numeric profile comparisons and guard

The SAME returned checked state fits the planned afterHead endpoint.
No numeric capacity follows from inclusion between unrelated alphabets.

This schedule deliberately has no SelectedValue normalizationProfile:
the current shared driver does not execute that phase. The prepared

Eight Shared*ScalarBounds/SharedNativeBranchBoundedResources modules

# Shared selected normalization: next cut

2026-11-09 19:14 CET. Read-only audit.

Source demand

Enumeration.hs:968-1018 runs stop/order/repetition, narrowing and the Right oracle BEFORE expansion. enumerateOutUVarWith:893-912 installs recursion ancestry, then expands exactly ONE outer Mu unfolding, or Node(nodeEdges n) for union. It clears ancestry and writes UVarEnumerated after expansion succeeds. Do not normalize before the Right oracle or repeat until ordinary.

Interned/Operations.hs:144-151 confirms one outer Mu layer; its result can remain Mu/union. nodeEdges:153-182 instead takes finite recursive/union closure, suppresses revisited identities, deduplicates/orders through Set, and raises on unresolved union Rec. enumerateNode:724-755 rejects Empty, defers nonterminal Mu/union into a slot, assimilates terminal endpoints, and raises on direct Rec. enumerateShallowHere/prepareShallowChild:791-809 defer eligible ordinary children. Missing model coverage does not imply a Haskell defect.

Current cut and reusable kernel

SharedRecursive.resume:136-167 runs SelectedStep.runPrefix, then only SharedSelectedContinuations.NativeOrdinaryContinuations.run. Its entry (:712-729) accepts a decoded .node without terminal trie; other entries yield None. SharedDispatch:55-93 performs assimilation/intersection/emptiness; SharedParent transforms a row. Neither supplies selected-root normalization.

Old SelectedContinuations.run:35-67, selected by PreparedRecursive.resume, prepares once and dispatches ordinary OR opaque/terminal expansion. Do not cast these executions to shared. Actual preparation is SelectedPreparation.run and SelectedPreparationResources.complete_resources.

SelectedValue.run:24-40 is a COMMON heap-only kernel: stored unfold for Mu, nodeEdges+makeNode for union, identity otherwise. It invokes no old Demand or shared conjunction. Reuse run_complete, SelectedValueCaller.complete/normalizationProfile/complete_resources, SelectedConstraintHeap.run_heap and preparation resource/arity/projectability laws. Caller.complete:55-77 uses current Context, native effects and memo growth; its old-named readiness helper is not an executed old call. Reuse this normalizer.

Prepared-head proof contract

R205 SharedNativeBranchResources.head_complete_resources:50-76 requires the captured handle to decode to the selected ordinary parent. Preparation keeps this slot/handle but can produce a DIFFERENT parent. Claiming that the old Mu/union handle decodes to that new .node would be false.

Raw SharedSelectedContinuations.CapturedEdge.run:523-531 already takes explicit edge and target, independently of parent lookup. SharedSelectedEdgeResources.complete_with_fragments_resources:48-60 already takes Available selectedParent, closed parent and selected row. Add a prepared-head producer with original ready/stored target and original decoded value, CURRENT available/closed prepared parent and selected row, plus prepared/original language equivalence for target semantics. Generalize the captured/head proof, not the stored identity. Finalize still writes the original target. Actual scalar observers already cover this executor and finalizeStopped.

Minimal next chain

1. Add SharedSelectedOpaqueDispatch +SharedPreparedContinuations. Capture ONE SelectedPreparation pair. On native done use its literal heap/entered cache; ordinary nonterminal values scan edgesOf(prepared) through shared NativeContinuations; remaining values use shared ChildDispatch and original-target finalization. Empty rejects. Preserve entry errors, pending/unresolved/exhausted fault heaps, terminal shared snapshots, stopped endpoints and finalizeStopped pre-finalize cache. No old executed wrapper.
2. Add prepared captured/head resources with the generalized contract above. CURRENT Packet, ready/stored slot and Fits/carrier derive SAME preparation/Post/Packet/RenderStable and result availability/closedness/language. Charge normalizationProfile once, then shared work from that endpoint. Keep captured handle, values, counter and waiting unchanged during preparation. Keep fourth/merge/query/global bundle unless an actual child changes it. No future result/cache ceiling supplier.
3. Add a prepared shared mixed reservation/recursive layer, then select it deliberately. Ordinary, terminal and opaque routes need their real schedules. Current ordinary-only finite resource laws do not cover them automatically. Keep callback-before-next-sibling and all failures.

Meaning and scope

Use exact language equivalence and entry Satisfies transport. Select edgesOf(prepared), not concatenated operand rows. Host correspondence still needs actual closure/dedup/order and interned identity linkage; language equivalence does not supply them. Source-policy/depth coverage, unrestricted unpaid Type annotations, complete enumeration and both signed inverses, fixed Word/Int adequacy, lazy tuple/requirement demand and host sharing remain separate obligations.

# Shared positive-depth composition

2026-11-09 19:18 CET. Read-only review of frozen composition and current SharedFiniteResources draft. No semantic defect found in the inspected coupling. Root owns compilation.

HookInduction.ResumeComplete:92 takes CURRENT Packet/Fits/carrier, edge membership/length, current mass and reservation. Its callback producer derives the actual Left result and framed Packet; Frame.values transports mass into that SAME cache. The continuing branch supplies the smaller-depth IH; rejection returns no outputs. FiniteResources.finite_complete discharges the IH by depth induction. No recursive completion supplier remains public.

FiniteHeadResources retains ONE captured-head receipt with its SAME caller, saved query, middleMemos/Post, bounds and stable observation. Complete cache mass comes from actual HeadCacheBounds. receipt_induction_complete_resources aligns advance(receipt) with reached caller/final.query before invoking the callback. completed_captured_packet derives a Packet for the ORIGINAL captured cache using that actual post.

FiniteSiblingResources runs callback/native recursion BEFORE the tail. Its tail receives hookCaller/hookMemos and restored captured cache. NativeContinuations.continued_head and the callback equation prove this order. It does not pass a callback-expanded enumeration cache into the next captured alternative. Outputs retain their actual cache/caller/query. Each existential full memo bundle belongs to its SAME endpoint/Post/query. The contract does not equate bundles across different outputs or larger-bound schedules, or claim a whole-driver ordered memo trace.

Unsupported .unhandled stops at actual ENTRY caller/query. Recursive stops retain their actual reason, outputs and optional endpoint. OutcomeResources allows endpoint=None; it does not manufacture a known endpoint. finalizeStopped keeps pre-finalize cache in executor/scalar observers. It is not Admitted, so sufficiently bounded admitted-head completion excludes it, rather than treating it as success.

PrefixResources derives actual heap-only prefix facts/Post from CURRENT Packet, with no external future Context/trace. Expansion threads that SAME post into entry/ordinary work. Nonordinary/terminal entries remain concrete unsupported stops. RecursiveReservation charges narrowSeed, then shared afterHead and smaller-depth work per sibling stage; the extra row covers parked recursion. It does NOT charge SelectedValue Mu/union normalization, consistently with the current ordinary-only run.

## Haskell finding and repair: component named filter

This is a VERIFIED implementation defect, not just a static concern. The old
decoder in cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Synthesis.hs around line 917 matched
application rows with at least two children and filter rows with at least one.
Actual generated Program application rows have EXACTLY four children:
[types, arrow marker, function, argument]. Actual generated filter rows have
EXACTLY two children: [goal, candidates]. Component and query argument rows
have EXACTLY one Type annotation child. All three source type encodings use
the same Program application and filter arities.

Before the repair, a component or argument called filter matched the broad
built-in filter pattern. Its Type annotation was decoded as a Program. The
public reproduction used an exported Library constructor with this input:

    typ = TCons "app" [TCons "A" [], TCons "B" []]
    lib = Library [("filter", typ, ["filter"])] [] [] FirstOrder
    query = Query [] typ
    source component size = 1

The accepted raw witness was filter[app[A,B],filter[app[A,B]]]. Freshly rebuilt
pre-fix public APIs returned solutionsOfSize = [App (Var "A") (Var "B")].
programsOfSize returned cardinality Right 1 and that same value. The decoded
component count was Right [2], although the requested source size was one.
A and B were not library components. The smart library normally renames its
component representatives. That does not restrict the exported constructor.
An ordinary query argument named filter can also reach the unary collision.
Both public roles now have regression checks.

The production repair changes only the two decoder patterns:

    ("app", [_, _, function, argument]) ->
      App (toProgram function) (toProgram argument)
    ("filter", [_, candidates]) -> toProgram candidates

The existing fallback preserves unary component and argument names as Var.
No reserved-name restriction, new dependency or caller premise is added.
The repaired public reproduction returns [Var "filter"], count Right 1,
values Right [Var "filter"] and decoded component counts Right [1].

Use the public Library constructor, Query, rawSearchSpace, solutionsOfSize and programsOfSize from cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Synthesis.hs. Here the outer filter is the built-in two-child goal check. The inner filter is the one-child component with its type annotation. There is exactly one typed term in the source language. Its intended Program is Var "filter", which has one component occurrence.

```haskell

import qualified Data.CFTA.Gen.Equality as G
import Data.CFTA.Gen.Synthesis
import Data.CFTA.Symbol (Symbol, symbolText)

leafCount :: Program -> Int
leafCount (Var _) = 1
leafCount (App f x) = leafCount f + leafCount x

main :: IO ()
```

## Explicit original-data forecast

Let A be GuardUniverse.guards of the ORIGINAL call heap. Let B be the ORIGINAL
algorithmic tuple budget and r the current constructor-heap Fits scalar.
The following functions use finite source data only:

```
s0 = max r (max B 1)
U(s) = Exposure.forecast s (ProjectionResources.jobsBound s s s s)
shape(A,s) = TupleBounds.shapeThrough A s
fresh(A,s) = RowsNumericControl.freshSize A s s
g(A,s) = 1 + max (U(s)) (2*s + shape(A,s) + fresh(A,s) + 2)
M = HeightOrderControlled.majorant (g A) (B+3) s0
P = StepNumericBounds.projectionFuel M
H = StepNumericBounds.readerFuel M
F = g(A,M)
```

P is the common projection ceiling. H is the common recursive reader ceiling.
F bounds the final quantitative profile. The full initial seed is at most F.
The functions are explicit mathematical definitions. The finite guard-shape
functions use classical finite bounds. These bounds can be extremely large.
They are not a practical memory estimate or an execution-time benchmark.
B remains the algorithmic tuple budget. It is not a source term-size request.

The fixed original guard carrier survives actual forcing and sampling.
Actual tuple shape gives raw tuple width equal to sampled operand width.
Rows derive their own normalized classes and exact new handle range. Cached
row length counts duplicate occurrences. Valid handles alone do not bound
that list length. Actual forcing cannot increase captured cell size.
Zero-fit table insertion is counted even when it consumes no tuple budget.

The actual budget above B+2 queue coordinates gives dimension B+3. Each
continuing transition derives a next Frame and a strict vector decrease.
The strict monotone growth function controls the current quantitative
profile. The actual successful Run is derived internally from readiness.
Its induction builds a controlled Path and exact same-state replay.
Path.final_le bounds its last scalar by M. The terminal transition gives F.
The proof compares actual steps at their computed local ceilings. It does
not assume that the computed ceilings exceed an old existential allowance.
Decision completion derives actual table read and table.length+1 growth.
Existing credit extensionality retains that exact decision at larger bounds.

SourceCurrentConjunctionSharedWorker.decision_total derives an actual shared
decision from the original query, original tuple budget, physical state,
and fixed native p/h. It returns a Boolean or the exact native shared
exploration fault. Pure table materialization and fixed-point growth cannot
produce an internal failure. No added work fuel, future completed table,
closure, heap, frame, rank, or read result is supplied. Open inputs return
false without native reads. Memo hits retain the original memo and physical
state. Successful misses alone insert the fourth memo. Failed misses retain
the exact fault and full private snapshot.

SharedWorkerEffects.decision_state/call_state identify the ENTIRE actual
snapshot. Closed decisions retain the actual explore endpoint; open inputs
and hits retain the initial empty-private snapshot. Misses retain the actual
decision endpoint. The read-free initial snapshot still has its unforced
initial query task. It need not be a drained execution.

SharedWorkerEffects.decision_effects/call_effects require only CURRENT
RowsAllocation.Ready and query availability. They derive physical Effects
and readiness, resident cached cell values, pending raw tuple edges, queued
conjunction operands, and stored table queries on ALL outcomes. They require
no closed query, future Ready, inventory, completion, or memo-correctness
supplier. They certify physical/value invariants. They do not certify the
stored Boolean of an arbitrary memo hit. Weaker existing branch laws remain.

RequirementPullSoundness.classConjunction_witness proves a semantic result
for an ACTUAL SUCCESSFUL class force. Initial closed/resident forests,
SemanticReady, CostHeap, annotation heap, nonempty forests, common accepted
child terms, and an active satisfied class derive a strictly smaller accepted
common subtree. Every projection comes from the literal singleton execution.
An accepted witness excludes first Empty. The proof does not fabricate a
complete eager graph. This is a conditional local soundness theorem; it does
not derive adequate native p/h or replace whole-call completion.

Updated: 2026-11-08 21:25 CET. This section is the current restart entry. All older
sections follow it without changes. The full formalization goal remains
active. Pushes to `formalize` remain authorized. Preserve unrelated `.hypha/`.

The top-level objective remains one source-grounded account of the optimized
interned worker and complete enumeration. It must cover actual callers,
generated siblings, reached states, failed paths, and subsequent calls. It
must include exact NODECOUNT counting, size and order, signed rank and unrank,
and correspondence with the Haskell implementation. Component results and
large mathematical resource bounds do not complete that objective.

## Current result

This checkpoint adds 13 modules and 36 public theorems. The main new endpoint
is `SourceCurrentConjunctionTuplePullNumeric.sample_complete`. Let `N` be the
original operand-list length and let `r` bound the initial heap. Define:

```
F = SourceCurrentConjunctionExposureResources.forecast N r
H = SourceCurrentProjectionUnionResources.readFuel F
```

Initial `Ready`, operand `Values`, `ClosedValues`, and `Fits r` derive a
completed physical sample at `H`. Every read allowance at least `H` returns
the same fit or overflow result and the same full physical state. The result
has the existing admission bound and input support. Returned rows and the
remaining cursor operands are closed. The final constructor heap satisfies
`Fits F`. The theorem takes no successful execution, future read trace,
future heap, or sufficient read allowance as a premise.

The proof first derives one successful execution from current facts. It
extracts its actual read sequence. It compresses actual successful prefixes
to their first demands. This gives the initial-support resource bound at
each read entry. The proof then replays the original sequence, including
repeated reads, at `H`. Exact cursor replay and the existing total-machine
observation inverse identify the same completed result and full state.
The computed allowance need not exceed the original witness allowance.

This endpoint concerns the physical demand sampler from R167. The selected
`SourceCurrentConjunctionTupleAdmission.run` still uses the eager exposure
path. The new endpoint does not change that definition. The later requirement
rows also retain their earlier eager model. These are open adoption tasks.

# 2026-10-29: graph text parser exception for strict-prefix equality paths

Status: REPAIRED and locally VERIFIED on integrated main `63aae675c`.
The integration commit is `e216346905cfeb0b243799138b4c254a739de0aa`.

With the lawful text codec `StateCodec id Right :: StateCodec Text`,
`parseGraphWith` throws for this input instead of returning `Left`:

```text
graph 1; start S; state S { a where equal([], [0]); }
```

The same failure occurs for `equal([0], [0, 1])` and both corresponding explicit
`constraint(CLASSES, true)` forms. Four focused cases throw the `toPathTrie`
strict-prefix exception. Four controls return graphs: empty classes, singleton
root classes, nonprefix paths and duplicate paths that collapse to one set entry.
The existing serialization test suite passed before this added coverage.

Cause: both parser branches call the `PathEClass` constructor before checking
whether a distinct path prefixes another. Its strict stored trie rejects that
representation with `error`. This concerns parsed text, not the Lean core model.

Repair: share a checked path-class parser. Deduplicate paths, inspect adjacent
paths in ascending order for a strict prefix, and report a parser error before
constructing the trie. Keep empty and singleton classes and exact valid stored
constraints. Extend the existing malformed-input list and document the format
restriction. No constructor or equality semantics change.

Focused reproducer: `/tmp/mcfta-prepared-ancestry-progress-20261029/serialization/repro-v1/PrefixClassException.hs`.
Run inside `nix-shell` with the host linker path:

```sh
export PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH
cabal exec -- runghc -package=cfta-serialization /tmp/mcfta-prepared-ancestry-progress-20261029/serialization/repro-v1/PrefixClassException.hs
```

Root recorded the original exception output under
`/tmp/mcfta-prepared-ancestry-progress-20261029/serialization-prefix-repro-before/`.
This probe catches exceptions and exits zero. Assess its eight labeled results,
not its process exit alone. After the repair, all four bad inputs return `Left`
and all four controls return graphs. The existing suite passes: 19 examples,
zero failures, with `-Werror`. Fourmolu and Cabal-gild checks pass. The exact
2,905-byte validation log has SHA256
`dee133f6b6001845390b5eb7a21b4fa500c1ef46a17533c8fcd0946101024bfb`.
All jobs ran serially in Nix under measured 4 GiB max/high and zero swap. The
first Nix build failed because its linker could not locate host `libgmp`;
prepending `/usr/bin` to `PATH` restored the host linker and the build passed.
This environment failure is separate from the reproduced parser exception.
No further Haskell repair is pending for this witness. The repair belongs to
`formalize`; upstream `main` does not yet contain it.

### E-graph cost context and lexicographic extraction progress

Main `82258094c` is integrated at `f61c306e7`. PR #183 changes the EGraph
extract and termsByCost cost callback to
`ClassId -> symbol -> [ClassId] -> [cost] -> cost`. Both the least-cost analysis
and actual row costs receive canonical owning and child class identifiers.
The generic FTA API retains its symbol-only callback. All 342 core examples
pass in Nix. The earlier constrained cost-5 witness still passes after adapting
only its callback arguments. The original reproducer remains unchanged.

A separate verified progress limitation predates this callback change.
Construct A = {a, u(A)} and a distinct singleton Z = {z}. Add bad(A,Z) with
the equality at paths [0] and [1]. Merge its class with the leaf good.
The class accepts good. Every bad(u^n(a),z) fails its equality.
For a lexicographic pair of Integer costs, take the maximum of all child
costs and a symbol base. The base is (1,0) for good and (0,0) otherwise.
Increment the maximum's second component. This cost is monotone and strictly
exceeds each child, including arbitrary negative input pairs.

The native acceptance check returns Right True for good. Ordinary size-based
extraction returns Just (1,good). The least-cost analysis returns Just (0,2).
The lexicographic extraction does not return within its internal two-second
timeout. Its exact 108-byte output has SHA256
`c0d16e5248c616734d370648f6ac58e313fccb2d327255adbb38dc8379779564`.
The source queue always has another cheaper bad candidate at cost (0,n),
before the accepted good at (1,1). This explains starvation. The timeout alone
is not a formal proof of nontermination.

The Haskell documentation repair `1c2e0cb21` states a sufficient progress condition:
each cost bound admits finitely many generated partial terms. It removes the
unsupported claim that local cost laws alone guarantee reaching a term.
EGraph.extract, both termsByCost interfaces, the internal search comment and
the changelog now record this limit. All executable Haskell expressions stay
unchanged by this repair. Changed Fourmolu and Cabal-gild checks pass in Nix.
External action: retain this regression and distinguish sorted returned
results from progress. No runtime repair or general extraction proof is claimed.

### Verified constrained EGraph.extract failure after main integration

Upstream `c168a952d779a72294c34d9c8fd5afd0e308c5ab` is integrated at
`646a9af8d543e53efbb08677840a15381afab8cc`. At that revision, EGraph.extract
promised the cheapest term of an e-class. Its implementation computed unconstrained
least costs, built only cheapest children, and then checked the parent path
equalities. It did not try a more expensive child after a failed equality.

Verified finite reproducer: merge g(a) and h(b) into C. Add p[C,b] with the
equality at paths [0,0] and [1]. Give h cost 2 + sum(children), and every other
symbol cost 1 + sum(children). The cost is monotone and exceeds each child.
The baseline native extract returned Nothing. Native termsByCost returned
p(h(b),b) at cost 5. Native classAutomaton accepted that term with Right True.
The cheaper unconstrained child g(a) failed the equality. All 341 existing core
tests passed. The earlier extraction property generated plain terms and missed it.

### Specftacular parallel completion follow-ups

Main `9d4e4d584aa7a681f075790e98466afe7531838a` is imported.
It adds finite completion fuel, optional parallel tests and speculation.
The default completion limit is 32768 consumed critical pairs. Zero is
unlimited. These changes do not modify native CFTA enumeration or Lean.
The six merged repairs in the table above remain unchanged.

`specftacular/src/Specftacular/Rewriting.hs:1113` waits for every speculative
worker. Line 1114 propagates every worker exception. The caller at lines
1078 to 1091 consumes decisions only through the first new equation, then
requeues all later pairs. Thus unused suffix work can raise an exception
or delay the earlier result. The retained exact-helper reproducer confirms
both cases. A serial prefix returns `Just ()`; a concurrent suffix error
raises `discarded suffix`. A blocked suffix prevents that prefix from
returning within 500 ms. These probes establish helper behavior. They do
not establish a failure of actual completion on valid finite terms.

Suggested external repair: consume results in input order through the first
`Just`, propagate only demanded-prefix exceptions, and cancel remaining
workers. Preserve every unconsumed pair for requeueing. If the current zip
interface stays, pad cancelled suffix decisions with `Nothing`. Truncating
the decision list alone would lose queued pairs. No repair is applied here.

Two further source-level concerns remain unvalidated at runtime.
`DecisionTree.hs:175` waits for all comparison chunks before selecting the
first difference; cancellation checks occur only between comparisons.
`Specftacular.hs:1357` discards enumeration worker identities and does not
stop surviving workers on caller cancellation. The latter helper now runs
in default phases 1 to 3. Public API liveness and worker cleanup need
focused reproductions before an external repair is claimed.

Source inspection found a possible overclaim in the new Typing.hs size-order
paragraph and cfta-generator README: "Binders generators already have
size-major ranks". fromTypingRules uses fromConstructorAutomaton, whose
route depends on actual graph cycles. An acyclic Binders grammar can use
finite constructor order. Candidate: Payload = P Payload | Z and T = A Payload | B Int, with only
rules A(value(P(P Z))) and B(value0), bound Binders0. Both roots have arity1.

valid external-field candidate did not reach rank output in the isolated
cached-dependency reproduction. Seven capped attempts retained compiler and
linker failures; the final executable aborted with exit134 and

- **Recursive field-pool repair: merged and locally validated.**
  Repair `b9219b9e` is merged by PR #65 at `c0cc8a05`. For
  `data Chain = End Bool | Next Chain`, a child pool containing `End False`
  could generate `Next (End False)` while `holds` accepted an invariant
  that requires `End True` at each Chain node. The repair rejects a field
  pool whose field type is the datatype being derived. It returns
  `FieldAtomOnDatatype "Next" 0` for that example. It does not silently
  filter the supplied subtree. Affected paths are
  `cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Refinement/Derive.hs`,
  `cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Refinement/Derive/Internal.hs`,
  `cfta-generator/test/Data/CFTA/Gen/Refinement/DeriveSpec.hs`, and
  `cfta-generator/CHANGELOG.md`. The new regression expects that error
  even with a trivially true invariant. The original executable counterexample
  remains in the preceding evidence directory, as recorded below.
  Local merge `896b0a1c` includes the repair. The strict Nix build and all
  798 examples plus golden pass. The unchanged original reproducer returns
  `Left (FieldAtomOnDatatype "Next" 0)`. Read
  `lean/restart-evidence/20261016-drawn-fields-local-worker/source-derive-self-field.log`.
  Its standalone `holds` checks remain `(True,True,False)`: this repair
  rejects the derivation configuration rather than validating opaque pool
  descendants. The new error and its validation order still need a source
  adapter. No additional local Haskell patch is added.
- **Negative typed-language bounds.** Upstream repair `443e3458` is included
  in PR #62 and main `999c04a5`. It changes
  `cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Typing.hs` and
  `cfta-generator/test/Data/CFTA/Gen/TypingSpec.hs`, with the corresponding
  entry in `cfta-generator/CHANGELOG.md`.
  Previously, `Nesting (-1)` and `Binders (-1)` could admit alternatives
  without subterm fields, as a zero bound does. The public
  `typingAutomaton` now rejects either negative bound with
  `NegativeBound bound` before it validates the node view. `fromTypingRules`
  uses that validation. Reproduce with `fromTypingRules @Arith
  (Typing bound [] [IntType] arithRules)`, where `bound` is `Nesting (-1)`
  or `Binders (-1)`. The regression "take a bound that is not negative"
  expects the corresponding error for both and no error for `Nesting 0`.
  The same commit corrects the environment-size documentation: with at most
  B binders in a field and nesting bound D, an environment has at most B * D
  binders. The three regression assertions pass in the current generator
  suite. No local repair is needed. The source adapter for this new error
  and its validation order remains open.
- **Recursive field-pool invariant: historical failure, fixed by b9219b9e.**
  This report describes the source before the repair recorded above.
  The statements below about an absent repair apply to that old source.
  Current main
  `999c04a5` accepts a field-specific pool for a field of the root datatype.
  The path was added in `d0966953`. With `data Chain = End Bool | Next Chain`,
  require `End True` at each Chain node and give Next's child the pool
  `[End False]`. `deriveLTAFrom @Chain 0` succeeds and enumerates
  `[End True, Next (End False)]`. The latter violates the independent
  all-node invariant, but `holds` returns `True`. The reproducer uses a
  lawful nonnegative `Literal Chain` encoding.
  Affected code is `cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Refinement/Derive.hs`
  (`fieldAtoms` and `evaluate`) and
  `cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Refinement/Derive/Internal.hs`

## Proof objective and open areas (2026-10-16)

The objective is to prove that the current Haskell library implements its
intended constrained tree languages and generators. Each public operation
has its own contract. There is no completed theorem for the whole library.

For an automaton A and node-count size n, exact queries must enumerate
exactly the distinct accepted terms of size n in the specified order.
Counts must equal the class cardinality. Rank and unrank must satisfy both
inverse laws. Finite queries must construct terminating evaluations.
Exact transformations must preserve the language. Merge, representative
selection, generator multiplicity, and sampling have separate contracts.

The exact Sized query laws are proved for successful modeled dispatch on
validated original graph rows. The finite ordinary reduction root constructs
a stable modeled execution and proves full guarded-language equality.

Its domain excludes Mu, references, and explicit unions.

Required stages, local reduction, and parents now construct their own
executions and constructor budgets from initial profiles and headroom.
Actual callback counts include Empty and repeated positions. Existing
universal prefix capacity plans follow from these initial bounds. Parent
returns the full actual outer caller receipt. The remaining composition

later parent entries.

Saturated target merging is **not monotone** under language inclusion or
source childwise row coverage. Five explicit pairs and a compact two-row
encoding have the same five native accepted terms. Both merge results are
already fixed points, but one accepts nine pairs and the other five.
`p(a,c)` separates them.

For a constrained language, compilation and enumeration must contain every
valid finite term and no invalid term. A finite FTA language with `n`
distinct terms must have exactly `n` ranks, with both decoder/inverse laws.
Sampling must give each term its requested normalized weight. An exact
optimization must preserve both the accepted language and the weights.

Three counts must remain separate:

- A **term** is one finite ordered constructor tree.
- A **run** is one accepting derivation. Several runs can produce one term.
- A **generator member** is one indexed source occurrence. Several members
  can have equal values and equal constructor terms.

The distinct-term rank contract applies to the FTA import path. Arbitrary
generator choices, maps, and joins retain members. They are not a quotient
by term or value equality. The checked recursive example
`label N (choice [pure, occurrence, occurrence])` has two size-two member
ranks with the same complete constructor term. Its inverse correctly returns
both ranks. This is a contract distinction, not a new decoder defect.

## Rebase integration and optimization coverage

The new upstream equality worker performs one pass. Its proof now describes
that operation directly. Explicit pruning and partial-reduction callers still
use fixed points where the source does. The formalization no longer attributes
an internal fixed-point loop to the public one-pass worker.

The classified similarity optimization preserves the exact ordered eligible
pair list and inference-error behavior. Its candidate comparison count is
the sum of `n * (n-1) / 2` over the classes. Classification, maps, and solver
costs remain separate. See [the similarity proof notes](lean/notes-similarity-within.md).

The indexed minimizer preserves the previous full-table schedule, including
root representatives and final copy passes. Installing a root representative
creates child links. The rebase integration now adds those parent-index
entries. Otherwise a later indexed copy could miss an inserted edge.
`MinimizeParentIndex` proves complete schedule equivalence and the required
metadata invariant. This is an integration obligation; it is not counted as
a separately reproduced public defect. See
[the parent-index notes](lean/notes-minimize-parent-index.md).

Retained size masses also move when constructors pay a size unit. Earlier
integration omitted those shifts in two paths. The source and transport
proofs now preserve the member/mass alignment.

The constructor record model omitted the current root self-reference filter.
`compileBody` now applies it at both probes and at the reserved binder identity.
The coherence, pending-record, and replay proofs include that reconstruction.
Kernel checks show that a recursive body with an added bare self operand
returns the same canonical record as the body without it. A second check
covers cleanup to an ordinary node. This repairs a source-correspondence
omission in the formalization; it is not a new Haskell defect. The lexical
`InternedBinderRebuild` and full `InternedSubstitution` worker now apply the
same filter. Their capture-avoidance, exact-language, free-reference, and
finite-allocation results remain proved.

## Recursive construction query repair

The pre-repair reproduction uses only public operations:

```haskell
recur $ \self -> case support self of
  Right EmptyNode -> oneof [pure 0, node "step" ((+ 1) <$> self)]
  _ -> leaf 99 "wrong"
```

Before the repair, the bound-three generator had four ranks and values zero through three,
each with probability one quarter. Its support rejects all four returned
engine terms. Count, sampling, and term rebuilds expose EmptyNode through
the placeholder; support reconstruction exposes its live recursive node.
The original public guardedness test accepts the body. The public API does
not state that a builder must avoid inspecting its argument.

The repair makes `support self` return `QueriedRecursiveOccurrence` in every
rebuild. The callback consistently returns the finite value 99. Its term
belongs to the returned support. Independent construction tokens remain
present during closed probes, which deliberately clear size-index flags.
The reproduction and pre-repair output are `/tmp/mcfta-context-builder.hs`
and `/tmp/mcfta-context-builder.log`; the repaired result is in
`/tmp/mcfta-context-builder-repaired.log`. The existing suite retains the
callback and the nested selected-key completion case.

This repairs the observed payload-query mismatch. It does not establish
regularity of every arbitrary callback or monotonicity of key discovery.
An empty family has no active records to reject. A callback can observe that
initial state and change its finite base after keys appear. Row 20 validates
the final discovered table before the source returns a tied family.

## Behavior that does not satisfy the stronger requested contract

**Similarity minimization preserves representatives, not every original
term.** Repairing root deletion does not make it an exact-language
optimization. A caller that requires all original expressions must not use
the representative theorem as a completeness theorem for the original set.

**Pool minimization does not preserve similarity-class probability.** It
starts a uniform distribution over the retained entries. The checked example
changes class masses from `2/3, 1/3` to `1/2, 1/2`. No discarded weight is
transferred to a representative. See
[the probability notes](lean/notes-pool-minimization.md) and
[the public reproduction](lean/repro/MinimizedPoolDistribution.hs).

**Unsupported or uncertain constraints are not empty languages.** General
quantified and nonlinear constraints lack a complete terminating solver
contract. The lattice backend rejects unsupported syntax, including `Ite`.
`Unknown`, timeout, unboundedness, and missing inspection fields remain
explicit states or errors.

**Logical alpha-equivalence does not imply identical solver verdicts.** A
sound name-sensitive callback can change `Yes` to `Unknown`. The supplied
adapter also rejects a generated actual name that collides with an unused
ambient declaration. No invalid term is admitted by that example. Exact
verdict preservation needs a name-transport/freshness contract. See
[the boundary notes](lean/notes-guard-alpha-boundary.md).

Efficiency has separate proof obligations. Balanced selection has checked
comparison/query bounds. Symbolic selection skips counted blocks, while
overlap preprocessing can be exponential. Polynomial evaluation and
arbitrary-precision arithmetic are not free. `groupBuilt` still enumerates
an already-built finite source during observation compilation.

The Lean sources are handwritten models and algorithm ports. The audit
checks their logical dependencies; it does not verify Haskell-to-Lean
translation. Source reproductions and finite probes support correspondence
but do not prove it for every runtime execution.

The complete physical **projected-leaf** schedule has a derived bound of the

order, empty propagation, and an allocation-free final fixed point in the

pullback and dead-row trimming prevent proof-prepared caches from becoming
runtime inputs. The physical intersection model now includes the source's
ordinary-node identity orientation. The path worker uses the exact ordinary

The 4,096 projected forests and 1,156 raw leaf source pairs pass again. See
[the runtime bound](lean/notes-equality-leaf-runtime-bound.md) and
[runtime trimming](lean/notes-equality-leaf-runtime-trim.md).

For one fixed **binary projected class**, `EqualityFixedProjectionInvariant`
proves that every original occurrence retains its rows after the first

occurrence-row pairs in a finite complete inventory. Nested endpoint rows are

### Other remaining source contracts

Typed nested-join families now connect support, diagnostics, both sampling
routes, weights, flags, complete inverse queries, and original occurrence
metadata. `RecursiveCompleteRecord` assembles those fields. Arbitrary opaque
Haskell builder schemas, key-discovery behavior, codecs, and lazy productivity
still require their stated contracts. Generator members remain distinct from
unique accepted FTA terms.

Full sparse Yes transports to complete logical satisfaction. Current pruning
and successful compiler classification inherit logical safety and exactness on
the success domain. A sound name-sensitive backend can still return sparse Yes
and complete Unknown. Exact backend-confirmed language equality requires
backend adequacy. The all-Int adapter derives its laws from correctly returned
external responses. See [logical read transport](lean/notes-source-read-logical.md)
and [the integer adapter](lean/notes-source-read-integer-adapter.md).

Runtime identity lifetimes, machine words, host containers, concurrency, lazy
productivity, solver IO, PRNGs, and user codecs retain explicit correspondence
contracts. There is no verified Haskell-to-Lean extraction. Similarity
minimization preserves representatives, and pool minimization starts a new
uniform distribution; neither implies exact term/mass preservation under the
stronger requested contract.

These boundaries prevent a whole-implementation verification claim. Resume
from [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md), using [NEXT-PROMPT.md](NEXT-PROMPT.md). Keep the
proof checkpoint, source fixes, and all restart material local.
